title: The Man Whose Belly Kept Growing — Jaundice, Swelling, and Twenty Years of Whiskey

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 45 years old, and he came to the hospital with three things that had been building for the same 20 days: a yellowish tinge to his eyes, a belly that kept swelling, and both feet ballooning with fluid. More recently, in just the last 15 days, he had also started feeling short of breath.

His story, though, really begins five years earlier. Back then, seemingly out of nowhere, he started vomiting and was hospitalized — and was told, for the first time, that he had low blood pressure, low potassium, and liver disease. He seems to have recovered enough to go on with his life. But recently, the same kind of illness returned, this time bringing jaundice with it. Twenty days ago, his abdomen began to distend, his eyes and urine turned yellow, and both his legs started swelling with pitting edema up to the knees.

He has no chest pain, no coughing up blood, no abdominal pain, and no urinary symptoms like burning or urgency. He has never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, asthma, or tuberculosis.

On taking a closer history, two habits stand out: he has been drinking about 360 mL of whiskey a day for the past 15 years, and chewing gutka (smokeless tobacco) for the past 10 years. He has no known drug allergies, and his appetite, diet, and bowel/bladder habits have otherwise been unremarkable.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General appearance:** conscious, coherent, cooperative; weight 53 kg, height 165 cm, BMI 19.4 — notably thin for his frame
- **Fluid status:** bilateral pitting edema up to the knees; icterus present
- **Vitals:** BP 110/70 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, RR 18/min, afebrile, SpO₂ 91% on room air, random blood glucose 138 mg/dL
- **Signs of chronic liver disease:** temporal wasting, loss of buccal and axillary fat pads, bilateral parotid enlargement, gynecomastia, palmar erythema
- **Respiratory exam:** dyspnea present; trachea central; vesicular breath sounds, no added sounds
- **Abdominal exam:** visibly distended abdomen (girth 85 cm), slit-like umbilicus, multiple old scars, visible distended veins over the abdominal wall, non-tender; mild hepatosplenomegaly on palpation; shifting dullness present on percussion, consistent with ascites; bowel sounds normal
- **Cardiovascular and neurological exam:** unremarkable
